newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa boss urges workers not to strike.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa boss urges workers not to strike.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber has written a letter to the airline's 50,000 staff urging them to vote against strike action in a ballot to be carried out by the trade union DAG from Tuesday.
A Lufthansa spokesman confirmed a newspaper report that Weber had sent a letter to its staff advising them of the possible harm to the company that an all-out strike could do.

White-collar worker union DAG, which shares representation of the airline's some 50,000 staff with the OeTV public sector and transport union, organised two limited walk-outs by staff late last year which cost Lufthansa tens of millions of marks.
A DAG spokeswoman confirmed earlier on Monday that balloting of its members would start from Tuesday and go on until February 25, after which a result would quickly be known.
If a full strike is to go ahead, the union needs to get the support of 70 percent of its members at the airline, which include ground, cabin and cockpit staff.

Lufthansa is offering a 1.7 percent annual wage rise, plus a one-off payment of 33 percent of a monthly salary and a payment of 500 marks ($306) cash or 625 marks in Lufthansa shares. A similar wage deal has already been signed with the OeTV union.
DAG wants a pay rise of around four percent and is unhappy with the duration of the 27-month contracts that Lufthansa wants its workers to sign.
